facts.statement: The generic name Heptasuchus combines the Greek word for 'seven' and the Latinized name of the Ancient Egyptian crocodile god.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from epta (ἑπτά), "seven" in Ancient Greek, and suchus (συχος) which is the Latinised form of the Ancient Greek word for the crocodile god of ancient Egypt.

facts.statement: The specific name 'clarki' honors George Clark of Casper, who discovered the type locality.
facts.quote: The specific name honors George Clark of Casper for discovering the type locality of Heptasuchus.

facts.statement: Most Heptasuchus specimens were thought to be lost until 1997, when it was confirmed they reside at the University of Wyoming, though some elements remain missing.
facts.quote: Thought to be lost until 1997, most of the specimens now reside at the University of Wyoming, although some elements are still unaccounted for.

facts.statement: Heptasuchus likely lived during the Carnian or late Ladinian stages of the Triassic, though the exact age is not precisely known.
facts.quote: The age of the type locality is not precisely known, but since it is lithostratigraphically equivalent to the lower Popo Agie Formation, though possibly chronostratigraphically older, it is probably Carnian or late Ladinian.

facts.statement: Heptasuchus possessed a long, straight pubis that was curved in anterior view and featured a pubic boot.
facts.quote: The hip had a long, straight pubis which was curved in anterior view and had a pubic boot.

facts.statement: Heptasuchus was a hypercarnivore that likely hunted or scavenged other animals in its environment.
facts.quote: Heptasuchus was a hypercarnivore and may have hunted or scavenged these animals and any others it came across.

facts.statement: Aggregations of Heptasuchus may indicate that these hypercarnivores dominated dwindling water supplies during droughts before succumbing to the conditions themselves.
facts.quote: Such aggregations are common among other loricatan genera (e.g. Batrachotomus, Decuriasuchus and Postosuchus) and predators in general (e.g. Allosaurus, dire wolf and modern alligators), suggesting that these animals, being hypercarnivores, may have dominated dwindling water supplies during drought before later succumbing to the drought themselves.

facts.statement: The fossil locality likely represents a drought assemblage, evidenced by weathered, disarticulated specimens confined to a small area.
facts.quote: The fossil locality probably represent a drought assemblage since the specimens are weathered, disarticulated, and confined to a small area that later served as a locus for deposition of water and sediment.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses suggest Heptasuchus is the sister taxon to Batrachotomus within the clade Loricata, supported by at least six shared character states.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis of archosaurs presented in an abstract found sister taxon relationship between Heptasuchus and Batrachotomus within Loricata, with a strong support of at least six shared discrete character states.

facts.statement: It was once hypothesized that Heptasuchus might be synonymous with Poposaurus, but this hypothesis has since been refuted.
facts.quote: It was suggested that Heptasuchus may prove to be synonymous with Poposaurus since they were both thought to be from the Popo Agie Formation, but this hypothesis has since been refuted.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Heptasuchus was an obligate quadruped or a facultative biped.
facts.quote: It is unknown whether this taxon was an obligate quadruped or faculative biped

facts.statement: Specimens of Heptasuchus were collected in the summer of 1977 from the newly discovered Clark locality northwest of Casper, Wyoming.
facts.quote: Recolectados durante el verano de 1977 en la por entonces recién descubierta localidad Clark al noroeste de Casper (Wyoming), los especímenes asignados a H. clarki fueron descritos en un breve artículo y dos tesis de maestría en la Universidad Estatal Wayne State en Detroit.

facts.statement: Heptasuchus was formally described and named by Robert M. Dawley, John M. Zawiskie, and J. W. Cosgriff in 1979, with Heptasuchus clarki as the type species.
facts.quote: Heptasuchus fue descrito y nombrado formalmente por Robert M. Dawley, John M. Zawiskie y J. W. Cosgriff en 1979 y la especie tipo es Heptasuchus clarki.

facts.statement: The genus name Heptasuchus is derived from the Greek words for 'seven' and the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva de epta (ἑπτά), "siete" en griego antiguo, y suchus (συχος) el cual es la forma latinizada de la palabra griega para el dios cocodrilo del antiguo Egipto, Sobek.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skull and partial postcranial skeleton (UW 11562), while paratypes include unassociated partial cranial and postcranial remains (UW 11563 to UW 11565).
facts.quote: UW 11562, un cráneo parcial y un esqueleto postcraneal parcial fue designado como el holotipo y los especímenes UW 11563 al UW 11565, que representan restos parciales craneales y postcraneales no asociados con el holotipo fueron designados como paratipos.

facts.statement: The specimens were thought to be lost until 1997, when many were found to be housed at the University of Wyoming, though some elements remain missing.
facts.quote: Se creyó que se perdió hasta 1997, y muchos de los especímenes ahora están alojados en la Universidad de Wyoming, aunque algunos elementos continúan desaparecidos.

facts.statement: The type locality dates to the Carnian or late Ladinian, based on its lithostratigraphic position below the lower part of the Popo Agie Formation.
facts.quote: La edad de la localidad tipo no se conoce con precisión, pero dado que es litoestratigráficamente a la zona inferior de la Formación Popo Agie, aunque es probablemente cronoestratigráficamente más antigua, así que debe datar del Carniense o finales del Ladiniense.

facts.statement: Heptasuchus was a medium-sized rauisuchian with a skull about 65 cm long and an estimated total length of 4.9 to 5.2 meters.
facts.quote: Heptasuchus era un rauisuquio de talla media, con un cráneo de cerca de 65 centímetros de largo y una longitud total estimada de 4.9-5.2 metros basándose en comparaciones con Batrachotomus.

facts.statement: Although no complete skull is known, preserved elements suggest Heptasuchus was similar to the German taxon Batrachotomus, featuring an arched nasal bone, a large naris, and a postorbital bar entering the eye orbit.
facts.quote: No se cconoce un cráneo completo, pero los elementos preservados indican que es un taxón muy similar a Batrachotomus de Alemania con un hueso nasal arqueado, una gran narina, y una barra postorbital que entra en la órbita ocular.

facts.statement: Reconstructions of Heptasuchus depict unusually large premaxillary teeth, based on a single premaxillary tooth that was partially erupted from its socket.
facts.quote: Las reconstrucciones de Heptasuchus representan a este con dientes premaxilares inusualmente grandes están basadas en un único diente premaxilar que estaba parcialmente salido del alveolo.

facts.statement: Heptasuchus possessed a long, straight pubis curved anteriorly with a pubic boot, and a slender ulna lacking the strong olecranon process seen in Postosuchus.
facts.quote: Tenía un pubis largo y recto, curvado en vista anterior, con una bota púbica, y un cúbito grácil que carece del fuerte proceso en el olecranon visto en Postosuchus.

facts.statement: Heptasuchus was originally assigned to the family Rauisuchidae based on shared traits with genera such as Prestosuchus, Postosuchus, and Saurosuchus.
facts.quote: Heptasuchus fue asignado originalmente a Rauisuchidae, basándose en las similitudes y rasgos compartidos con géneros como Prestosuchus, Postosuchus y Saurosuchus.

facts.statement: Zawiskie et al. (2011) diagnosed Heptasuchus using two autapomorphies: large, posterodirect flanges on the parabasisphenoid and a distinctive postfrontal projecting from the orbit.
facts.quote: Zawiskie et al. (2011) diagnosticaron a Heptasuchus basándose en dos autapomorfias, rasgos anatómicos que lo diferencian de todos los demás arcosaurios conocidos; la presencia de grandes flancos grandes y dirigidos posteriormente en el parabasisfenoide y un distintivo postfrontal sobresaliendo de la órbita.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis suggested Heptasuchus and Batrachotomus are sister taxa within the group Loricata, supported by at least six shared discrete character states.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético presentado en un resumen encontró que Heptasuchus y Batrachotomus serían taxones hermanos dentro del grupo Loricata, con un fuerte fundamento en al menos seis estados de características discretas compartidos.

facts.statement: The fossil locality likely represents a death assemblage caused by drought, as specimens are weathered, disarticulated, and confined to a small area that later became a water and sediment deposition site.
facts.quote: La localidad fósil probablemente representa una asociación producida por una sequía dado que los especímenes están desgastados, desarticulados y confinados a un área pequeña que más tarde sirvió como un lugar para la deposición de agua y sedimentos.

facts.statement: Fully disarticulated and showing subaerial weathering, Heptasuchus remains are found alongside small, unidentified archosaurs and phytosaurs (represented by teeth and possible skeletal elements, or in one case, a nearly complete series of vertebral centra).
facts.quote: Completamente desarticulados y con signos de desgaste subáereo, los restos de Heptasuchus aparecen junto a los de arcosaurios pequeños y sin identificar y fitosaurios (representados por dientes y posibles elementos del esqueleto o en el caso del pequeño arcosaurio, una serie casi completa de centros de vértebras).

facts.statement: Heptasuchus was a hypercarnivore that likely hunted or scavenged on other animals.
facts.quote: Heptasuchus era un hipercarnívoro y puede haber cazado o devorada la carroña de estos animales y de otros que se encontrara.

facts.statement: Because multiple individuals are represented in a single locality, it has been suggested that Heptasuchus may have lived in groups.
facts.quote: Dado que varios individuos están representados por el tipo el material referido en una única localidad, se ha sugerido que Heptasuchus puede haber vivido en grupos.

facts.statement: It is debated whether all pseudosuchian elements from the locality belong to Heptasuchus; while Wroblewski (1997) suggested the taxon was a paleontological chimera, Zawiskie et al. (2011) argued it is not.
facts.quote: Zawiskie et al. (2011) sugirieeron que todos los elementos de pseudosuquios recolectados en la localidad pertenecen a Heptasuchus y que el taxón no es una quimera paleontológica como fue sugerido anteriormente por Wroblewski (1997).

facts.statement: Heptasuchus lived during the Carnian stage, approximately 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists Heptasuchus as belonging to the parent group Poposauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Poposauridae
